item.title: Food Tour and History Walk of Montclair — Sat Aug 22, 1:00 PM — Crane Park
item.description: Explore Montclair, NJ on this immersive food tour showcasing a hyperlocal culinary hotspot, co-hosted by Chow Town Food Tours and Montclair History Center. “Montclair In Motion” is a social, flavorful experience rooted in this colorful community’s unique industrial history and more recent cultural growth, including culinary traditions from Argentina, the Philippines, Sicily, West Africa, and Brazil. Chow Town Food Tours and the Montclair History Center will provide expert insights for a tour to remember. This guided exploration of Bloomfield Avenue will lead guests on a leisurely one-mile walk, stopping for Brazilian comfort food, humongous cookies, and more. Meet the chefs and business owners that make this one of the most exciting restaurant scenes in the state. Discover the hidden history behind architecture, landmarks, and other notable highlights from the experts at the nonprofit Montclair History Center. Bring an appetite! item.title: Shorebirds with the Man Who Wrote the Book — Tue Aug 25, 7:30 AM — NJ
item.description:
Spend two days experiencing some of the east coast’s best shorebirding with Michael O’Brien, one of the authors of “The Shorebird Guide”! The Shorebird Guide, Houghton Mifflin’s landmark title on the subject, is authored by three Cape May birders and your guide for this workshop is one of them. Experience the best shorebirding on the East Coast with Michael O’Brien, equal parts skilled birder, expert guide and superb teacher. We’ll search South Jersey’s best shorebird locations in search of sandpipers, plovers, yellowlegs, and hope to find a few other gems such as phalaropes or godwits. Over 25 plover and sandpiper species are within reach, and some species number in the thousands here at this time of year. Begin learning identification by size, shape, behavior and voice, then move on to careful examination of plumage details, as The Shorebird Guide outlines.

item.title: Memory Café - A Dementia-Friendly Social Gathering — Mon Oct 12, 11:30 AM — Montclair Main - Auditorium
item.description:
For adults with dementia and their caregivers, this event offers a welcoming, safe, calming space for socializing, music, art and reminiscing every month.
A “Memory Café” is a dementia-friendly social gathering for individuals with early-stage memory loss or mild cognitive decline and their care givers.
The meetings will be held in a safe and comfortable environment where people can interact and socialize with others having similar experiences. At the gatherings participants can get support in a non-judgmental setting, while enjoying the benefits of music for the brain.
The meetings will be run by Lisy Espindola, LCSW and Kim McLennon, MSW and music therapist. Lunch and/or snacks will be served.
This is a joint program between Lifelong Montclair at the Township of Montclair and the Montclair Public Library.
Attendance is free but registration is required. Questions? Call 973-744-3278.

item.title: Singles Padel Mixer — Meet Someone in Hillsborough NJ (Beginners) — Sun Aug 23, 11:30 AM
item.description: North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis & More A singles mixer that isn't standing around a bar making small talk. If you're single in New Jersey and tired of the apps, come meet other single people the easy way — by actually doing something together. We're playing padel: the fast-growing, genuinely social racket sport that's easy to pick up. No experience, no partner, and no equipment needed — you show up solo, we hand you a racket, and an instructor gets you playing in minutes. Then we run rotating games, so you meet different people all afternoon instead of getting stuck with one partner. Everyone's missing shots for the first twenty minutes — that's the point. It's a far easier icebreaker than "so, what do you do?", and conversation just happens because you're doing something together. item.title: LINES TO LOVE: Screen-Free Afternoon with Your Child — Sat Oct 3, 1:00 PM — The Space
item.description:
Lines to Love: A Creative Space for You & Your Child. Led by Leo A. Sante Remember what it felt like to simply be together with the child you love?
No screens, no rush, no expectations.
Just being side by side, doodling, making up stories, letting your imaginations wander wherever they wanted to go. Lines to Love brings you back to that space. Using a simple roll of paper and a few drawing materials, you and your child will be guided into a playful world of co-creation. Together, you’ll follow lines, add to each other’s doodles, build whimsical stories, and let the drawing become a pathway to imagination. Lines to Love is inspired by a cherished ritual between a father, Leo, and his young son, Lucas. Back when Lucas was little, Leo would just roll out paper and two pens. Together they’d spend hours just doodling, creating, and enjoying the precious time together. Both Leo and Lucas cherish those drawings and those moments to this day. item.title: Everything Book Club, "The Ministry of Time" by Kaliene Bradley — Tue Oct 6, 1:15 PM — Montclair Main - Tower Room
item.description:
An instant New York Times bestseller. In the near future, a new government ministry is exploring time travel. Our heroine gets a highly paid job assisting and monitoring the time travel expat known as “1847” or Commander Graham Gore. As far as history is concerned, Commander Gore died on a doomed 1845 expedition to the Arctic, so he’s a little disoriented by living with an unmarried woman who regularly shows her calves, uses outlandish devices such as “washing machines” and “Spotify,” and talks about “the collapse of the British Empire.” This witty, sexy, genre-bending debut novel will tug your heartstrings, make you laugh, and ultimately make you think.
"A hilarious yet poignant take on dislocation, loss, and oddball community . . . A twisty plotline that incorporates plenty of John le Carré and Mick Herron spy-craft references . . . with the silly, incisive, and spot-on comedy of Douglas Adams."—The Boston Globe

item.title: Breaking the Silence: Understanding Depression, Suicide, and the Power of Connection — Wed Oct 7, 6:00 PM — Montclair Main - Auditorium
item.description:
Presentation by Dr. Jason Dean and Dr. Rae Dumont
Depression is often misunderstood, accompanied with shame, secrecy or blame. So is suicide. The impact a loss by suicide has on friends and family is enormous. Without open conversations, people often feel alone as they carry the memory and question themselves about what they might have done to help.
This presentation, in the context of a rising incidence of depression, anxiety and suicide, aims to offer understanding and compassion for people who struggle with mental illness. It offers insights and comfort to those who have loved a person with depression, and tried to help.
There will be ample time for discussion and for questions.
Rae Dumont, MD, LMFT, is both a pediatrician and a family therapist. While she practiced and taught at Harvard Medical School, she focused on the impact of one person's illness through the entire family, and on the interconnection between mental and physical health.

item.title: NJ Code & Coffee - Newark Tech Week edition — Sat Oct 17, 2:00 PM
item.description:
NJ Code & Coffee Calling all New Jersey techies to the **NJ Code and Coffee** tech community meetup at the EqualSpace ES550 Tech & Innovation campus during Newark Tech Week!
Code and Coffee is an inclusive, informal networking/co-working session for those in tech (and the tech-curious). That includes operators, founders, and investors. Developers, data engineers, UX/UI designers, data scientists, product managers, software engineers, solution architects... **all are welcome!**
People of all skill and experience levels can attend, we love it that way. Many people (optionally) bring projects to work on, and many other people (optionally) socialize the entire time. It's entirely up to you!
Come grab a cup of coffee and meet new people, share stories, find collaborators, talk about everything tech, talk about everything NOT tech, take a break from job applications, get away from the computer screen, make connections, make conversation, **make friends!**
**Agenda:** **2pm:** Doors open,
